title: Invariant symmetric-power lifting under quotients and extensions
statement:
For a commutative ring $A$ and a flat affine finitely presented group scheme $J$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, put $A[J]=\Gamma(J,\mathcal O_J)$. A rational $J$-module is an $A$-module $M$ with coaction $\rho:M\to M\otimes_A A[J]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities for the coordinate Hopf algebra; an invariant satisfies $\rho(m)=m\otimes1$, and an equivariant map commutes with coactions. Define $P(A,J)$ to mean that for every rational $J$-module $M$ and every equivariant surjection $\lambda:M\twoheadrightarrow A$ to the trivial module there are $n\geq1$ and $q\in(\operatorname{Sym}_A^n M)^J$ with $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\lambda)(q)=1$. Here $\operatorname{Sym}_A^n M$ is the degree-$n$ piece of the free commutative $A$-algebra on $M$, with its induced coaction and $\operatorname{Sym}_A^n A\simeq A$. No finiteness or flatness is assumed for $M$. Group schemes and homomorphisms use the group-object diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over the indicated affine base [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; affine, finite presentation, flatness, tensor product and symmetric algebra have the meanings of [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property, lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. Let $K,H,Q$ be flat affine finitely presented group schemes over $A$ in an exact sequence
$$1\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow H\xrightarrow{\pi}Q\longrightarrow1.$$
Exact means that $K$ is the scheme-theoretic kernel $H\times_{Q,e_Q}\operatorname{Spec}A$, that $\pi$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation, and that $Q$ represents the quotient sheaf $H/K$ for the fppf topology (covers are jointly surjective families of flat locally finitely presented maps). Then $P(A,H)$ implies $P(A,Q)$, and $P(A,K)$ together with $P(A,Q)$ implies $P(A,H)$. Kernels need not be smooth or reduced.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5(2),(5), pp.522-523, and Proposition 9.5.1(i),(ii), printed p.525. This is the symmetric-power formulation, not a restriction to finite free representations. Local PDF WANTED; read https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf

proof.text: Assume $P(A,H)$. Given a rational $Q$-module $M$ and an equivariant surjection $\lambda:M\twoheadrightarrow A$, inflate along $\pi$. This keeps the underlying map and its surjectivity. The induced symmetric-power coaction is also the inflation of the $Q$-coaction: both are obtained by extending the coaction on $M$ multiplicatively, and hence agree by the symmetric-algebra universal property. Apply $P(A,H)$ to obtain $n\geq1$ and an $H$-invariant $q\in\operatorname{Sym}^n M$ mapping to $1$. Inflation detects invariants by [lem-sfb-normal-kernel-invariants-quotient-action], so $q$ is $Q$-invariant. This proves $P(A,Q)$.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5(5), pp.522-523, and Proposition 9.5.1(i),(ii), p.525; direct rational-module argument for its quotient/extension assertions.

proof.text: Now assume $P(A,K)$ and $P(A,Q)$, and take an arbitrary rational $H$-module $M$ with equivariant surjection $\lambda:M\twoheadrightarrow A$. Restrict its coaction along $K\to H$. The same map is a surjective $K$-map, so the definition of $P(A,K)$ gives $n\geq1$ and $q\in(\operatorname{Sym}^n_A M)^K$ with $\lambda_n(q)=1$, where $\lambda_n=\operatorname{Sym}^n(\lambda)$.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5(5), pp.522-523, and Proposition 9.5.1(i),(ii), p.525; direct rational-module argument for its quotient/extension assertions.

proof.text: Put $V=\operatorname{Sym}^n_A M$ and $N=V^K$. By [lem-sfb-normal-kernel-invariants-quotient-action], $N$ is a rational $Q$-module and the restriction $\mu=\lambda_n|_N:N\to A$ is $Q$-equivariant (the invariant module of the trivial target is $A$ with its trivial action). It is surjective since $\mu(aq)=a$ for every $a\in A$. Apply the definition of $P(A,Q)$ to obtain $m\geq1$ and $r\in(\operatorname{Sym}^m_A N)^Q$ with $\operatorname{Sym}^m(\mu)(r)=1$. Arbitrary modules are permitted, so no finiteness or flatness of $N$ is needed.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5(5), pp.522-523, and Proposition 9.5.1(i),(ii), p.525; direct rational-module argument for its quotient/extension assertions.

proof.text: Extend the inclusion $N\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^n_A M\subseteq\operatorname{Sym}_A M$ to an algebra map $F:\operatorname{Sym}_A N\to\operatorname{Sym}_A M$ by the universal property. A product of $m$ generators maps to a product of $m$ degree-$n$ elements, hence to degree $nm$ by the grading statement; these products span $\operatorname{Sym}^m N$. Denote the restriction by $\theta:\operatorname{Sym}^m N\to\operatorname{Sym}^{nm}M$. It is $H$-equivariant: the two coaction composites of $F$ are algebra maps agreeing on each generator, since $N\hookrightarrow V$ is equivariant; uniqueness makes them equal. Similarly, on every product $x_1\cdots x_m$, one has $\lambda_{nm}(\theta(x_1\cdots x_m))=\prod_i\lambda_n(x_i)=\prod_i\mu(x_i)$, and linearity gives $\lambda_{nm}\theta=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\mu)$. Inflating the invariant $r$ gives an $H$-invariant; thus $\theta(r)$ is $H$-invariant and maps to $1$. Since $nm\geq1$, this proves $P(A,H)$.
